history.replaced_because: spec v3 (post hoc: chosen after seeing the 0.5% and 2% results): the shares 1%, 3%, 5% and 10% are added; tracebed.py gains the post-hoc shares, their labels, the spec each share's outputs must name and a guard that refuses writes into spec-v2 outputs; run_job.py refuses spec-v2 shares, labels post-hoc records and writes pooled_v3.json with the map over every share; launch.sh takes explicit CPUs (checked), runs the post-hoc shares and logs to logs/v3_*; checks_v3.py is new; checks_seed0.py refuses under spec v3; write_spec.py gains the append-only v3 path; test_trace.py covers all of it. signals.py is unchanged.

after the first run of checks_v3.py (passed; moved to superseded/v3_checks_run1): checks_v3.py keeps the smoke step's own progress lines (tiny-setting losses and flag levels) out of the log, as its record states; run_job.map_lines prints full origin and usable labels. No trained job exists; spec v3 is unchanged.

review finding (minor), before any trained job: launch.sh accepted any CPU taskset could pin to, including CPUs 2 and 3, which run the stand-ins and must not be used, and run_job.py's usage example named CPU 3. launch.sh now allows only CPU 0 or CPU 1 (CPUs 2 and 3 are refused before anything is pinned, written or run) and checks the second CPU of 'all' before the logs folder is made; run_job.py's example names CPU 1; checks_v3.py adds the refusal of CPUs 2 and 3 to its refusal checks, runs every launch refusal dry (stub interpreter, scratch output folder, a taskset on PATH that records the CPU asked for), and states the CPU load neutrally; test_trace.py tests that 'all 0 1' pins only to CPUs 0 and 1 and that every launch naming CPU 2 or 3 is refused. Spec v3 is unchanged: the new refusal adds to what it says about the launch. The second run of checks_v3.py moved to superseded/v3_checks_run2.
